# Online marketing strategy for your GYM

### Lets get you started !!!

[![Gym Marketing on GMB](/uploads/1/2/7/6/127602180/editor/gmb.jpg?1585139113)](https://dublindigitalagency.weebly.com/uploads/1/2/7/6/127602180/gmb_orig.jpg)

If you are a gym owner and looking for a perfect online gym marketing solution for your gym, then you landed in the right place. Here we will tell you, how you can engage with your potential customers for “FREE”, yes you heard it right. With google my business you can make your business profile for free and connect to customers around google search (world’s favorite search engine) and maps. You can add pictures or offers related to your business into your profile. GMB helps your customers reach you by providing options like calling, email, website, and maps. Your customer can also post feedback in the reviews section, which can help you with building a positive image(Google My Business, no date).

As per bright local study(Murphy, 2019), 84% of the searches are discovery searches, which mean people are searching for a particular category, product or service you are providing and your business will appear. More than 50% of customers visit the website after finding a business on GMB, more than 20% of calls and rest look for direction. 
If you are a gym owner, the study also found that more than 120 visits per month on a fitness related website and 30% people request for direction.
 
If this doesn’t impress you to go for GMB, read this, local businesses receive more than 90% of phone calls from GMB.
 
Follow these simple steps and enter the world of online gym marketing by making your business profile on GMB to reach your customers on google who search for your product and services every day and I will provide you with some helpful tips on how to increase your business visibility on google search with local SEO.
​
**Steps to setup your GMB profile:**

* Go to google.com/business 
* Sign in with your business google account (if you don’t have then you can create one)
* Enter your business name
* Enter your name, address and phone number
* Enter your link to the website
* Chose category for E.g. if you are a gym owner, please select categories related to fitness.
* Verify your information through various methods provided by GMB. 

 
**Tips to optimize your Gym’s Google My Business visibility:**

**1\. Optimize GMB Page:** Make sure your GMB page is filled with all the information such as NAP(name, address and phone number), categories ( Gym – CrossFit, personal trainer, fitness centre), add a short and precise description about your Gym or fitness centre along with CTA, mention operating hours and images of your gym as per google, business with photos receive more than 40% more request and more than 30% website visits(Main Street ROI, no date).   

**2\. Improve your local SEO:** Local SEO as the name suggests helps businesses to target local customers for their products and services. Local SEO is different from broader SEO as search engines focus more on local content, citation, social pages and links(Smith, no date).  

* Search for relevant keywords related to your business product or services e.g. CrossFit training, 24hrs gym, etc. You can make a free AdWords account and use their free tool “keyword planner” to look for suitable keywords and optimize your GMB page and your website (Main Street ROI, no date).
* You can optimize your GMB page by keeping all the information up to date, add as much information as possible related to identified keywords.
* You can optimize your website for local SEO by adding a google map to your contact us page, create local content by writing blogs and optimizing blogs for local audiences, make your website more mobile-friendly (Smith, no date). 

  **You can learn more about SEO for your website** **[here](https://dublindigitalagency.weebly.com/blog/local-seo-strategy-tips)**.

 **​3.** **Link GMB to Google AdWords account**: If you are running an ad campaign through Google AdWords, integrating GMB with AdWords can increase your gym or fitness center ad visibility and impressions. This collaboration will allow you to do more location base targeting, which is good for your gym or fitness center(Davidson, 2017).   Can learn more about Google AdWords [here](https://dublindigitalagency.weebly.com/blog/google-ads-to-boost-gym-memberships).

**4\. Leverage Reviews:** Reviews give your business proof of authentication. As per Imaging someone looking for a gym near their location and they come across several search results. The customer tends to check reviews made by other people before making their mind to visit your gym or not. Positive reviews are always good for your gym but even if you have a negative review, you should always respond to them and this will show that you are responsive to feedback.  More than 90% of people read reviews and more than 85% make their decisions based on the reviews (Technogym, 2018).
Reviews don’t show up overnight, you can request your existing clients to leave unbiased reviews on your GMB listing and always encourage new clients to leave their valuable feedback (Jones, 2019).

* Less cost-effective. 
* Reach your potential customers who are geographically situated close to your gym or fitness centre.
* Ratings and reviews will help you gain the trust of your future clients and will also help your business to appear on top of the SERP. ​

# How to Start Social Media Marketing for your Fitness Studio or Gym in 6 Simple Steps

December 11, 2020 | [3 Comments](https://blog.appointy.com/2020/12/11/social-media-marketing-for-fitness-studio-gym/#comments)

A couple of years back, social media was considered the younger, cooler kid on the block in the small business marketing domain. But as digital overtook the more conventional modes of marketing, now it’s an important way for all businesses – including fitness studios, gyms, and fitness centers to bring in new clients!

**But, like any other marketing initiative, to stand out amongst millions of other brands and drive actual sales, you need a well-crafted social media marketing plan for your fitness business.**

In this blog, we will guide you through the steps on how to get started with social media marketing for your fitness studio or gym. 

Keep in mind that this blog is for fitness business owners, professionals, and personal trainers who want to start experimenting with social media for their gyms or fitness centers.

If you already have a decent presence on social media and want to optimize it, you might want to check out our advanced social media marketing series – due to launch soon. You can leave your email address below to receive it directly in your inbox. 

* * *

## **How to start promoting your fitness business on social media in six simple steps**

Here are a few tips on how to promote your gym and fitness business on social media:

* * *

### **1\. Keep it lean and start organic** 

Before you go and hire a social media manager, start by yourself and see how well it works. Investing money in fitness social media marketing will make sense once you have your goals and plans in place, but you can only be sure about this once you start testing the waters.  

Many might advise you to hire an expert to take advice or to create a social media plan before getting started, but before you go about doing that, first you need to have a clear understanding of how your target audience engages with social media and what message would you like to send. 

**Experiment with it yourself first and then slowly scale it up so that you have the right answers to questions like what do I want to achieve from social media, who should I target, and which platform to use.** 

Also, while experimenting, do not get tempted to jump straight to paid social media marketing for your gym or fitness center. It might give you results in the short term, but it’s not sustainable for long-term fitness business growth. Make sure that you have learned how to take advantage of the free elements of social media like post sharing, comment engagement, community building, etc. before you venture into paid advertising.

* * *

### **2\. Look at fitness brands and businesses that are winning social media** 

The best way to figure out the low-hanging fruits to capitalize on is to find out what your counterparts and the influencers in the fitness community are doing – what’s working for them has a good chance of working for you too with a few tweaks. 

If you are new to fitness social media marketing, this is the single most important exercise you can do before stepping in the ring yourself, so don’t cut back on the effort here. Think of this as a social media campaign you’re running for your fitness studio! Here is how to go about it: 

*   Start by making a list of about 15-20 businesses or brands that you hear a lot about. You can start right at the top by checking out big fitness brands like Nike Women, Gold’s Gym, etc. Other than this, you can also include some local influencers and gyms in your area. Keep adding more names to this list as you find more related pages or suggested people depending on the network you are on. 

*   Visit each one of the profiles on your list across popular social networks like Instagram, Facebook, Youtube, Twitter, even LinkedIn. Note the following things about them: 
    *   Profile description 
    *   Post cadence (how often and when do they post) 
    *   Post type (Motivational, service-related, Memes, etc.)
    *   Caption style 
    *   Average post views and engagement (likes, comments, shares)
    *   Quality of posts 
    *   Follower count

*   Once you have this data, understand which social media platforms are these businesses more active on. This will give you a tentative idea of where your audience spends most of their time, and hence, where you should focus first. 

*   Also, the follower count and engagement numbers will help you set your initial goals realistically. Social media platforms often see little follower-to-engagement ratios but still drive results in the background. 

* * *

### **3\. Create your social media profiles** 

Do not rush through this step. The information you enter on your business’s social media page can be vital in casting the right impression on potential leads. While it involves simply filling out a few form fields, getting this right the first time will help you get the most out of any effort you put into promoting your profile. 

Here are a few tips to help you market your gym/ fitness center on social media: 

*   **Finalize the name for your social media profile.** It’s ideal to name it after your business but if you think your personal brand might impact the initial exposure for your business, feel free to use it. Just keep in mind that it’s really important that you use the same name across all your social media profiles. This helps create a uniform brand image for your business. 

*   **Refrain from using a mid-workout selfie as your profile picture, and use a high-quality image.** For profile pictures, it might be alright to use different ones keeping in tone with the different platforms. If applicable, add a cover image as well that complements the color palette of the platform and looks good. Keep in mind that all social media profiles have specific guidelines on the image upload dimensions. Follow them to ensure that your pictures look good in thumbnails as well. 

*   **Add a profile bio/ description that covers key points about you and your experience.** You might want to add special mentions, achievements, or past experiences/ trainees that might help increase your credibility. Take inspiration from other health and fitnes

Affiliate Gym

Starting a gym is a thrilling challenge. Are you ready to embark on this exciting journey? 

With the right guidance, this adventure becomes both rewarding and successful. A good startup [guide](https://zenplanner.com/resources/guides/) is essential for navigating the complex path of opening a gym. 

This gym owner setup guide covers everything from creating a business plan to advanced marketing strategies, ensuring you have the tools to build a thriving gym business. Ready to turn your dream into reality?

## 1\. Why a Comprehensive Gym Startup Guide is Essential

Starting a gym requires careful planning. A comprehensive gym startup guide is the cornerstone of success. It provides crucial insights and detailed instructions to navigate through the nuances of launching and managing a gym. Moreover, by following a structured plan, you minimize risks and position your business for long-term growth. 

Think of it as your roadmap. 

This guide outlines the key steps to take—from securing the right location to understanding the financial investments needed to establish a successful gym—and offers practical advice for each stage. 

Additionally, a well-crafted guide ensures you understand industry trends and best practices, positioning you to excel in 2024 and beyond. With this [resource](https://zenplanner.com/resources/), you’ll confidently tackle any challenges and unlock opportunities, driving sustainable business growth. 

## 2\. Creating a Gym Business Plan

Developing a solid business plan is crucial for the success of your gym. A detailed business plan serves as your guide, outlining every aspect of your gym’s operations and growth strategy. It sets the foundation for your business and helps attract investors. 

Start by defining your gym’s vision and mission. Clearly articulate what you aim to achieve and the unique value your gym will provide to the community. 

Next, conduct a market analysis to identify your target demographic, analyze competitors, and recognize potential opportunities. This research will help shape your marketing and operational strategies. 

With a well-structured business plan, you will have a clear roadmap to follow, ensuring you stay focused and aligned with your goals. 

#### [**Read more on** **How to Open a Gym**](https://zenplanner.com/gymowner/how-to-open-a-gym/)

## 3\. Understanding Gym Startup Costs

Before opening a gym, understanding startup costs is crucial to ensure financial stability and success. These expenses can include anything from a commercial space lease, equipment purchase, staffing, and marketing, to smaller essentials like utilities and [software](https://zenplanner.com/product/member-self-service/). It’s important to create a detailed list of these anticipated costs to avoid surprises and ensure a well-rounded budget. 

Additionally, many prospective gym owners overlook the administrative costs involved. This includes permits, licensing, and insurance, which are critical to maintaining legality and safety standards in your facility. 

By thoroughly researching and documenting all potential expenses, aspiring gym owners can develop a comprehensive financial plan that anticipates both inevitable and unforeseen costs. This foresight paves the way for smoother operations and a clearer path to profitability, positioning the business for long-term success. 

#### [**Check out our complete** **financial guide** **for your fitness business**](https://info.zenplanner.com/gym-financial-management?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fzenplanner.com%2F%7D)

## 4\. Developing a Gym Management Budget

Creating a detailed budget is essential for your gym’s long-term financial health, ensuring you allocate resources wisely, manage cash flow, and prepare for unexpected expenses. Budgeting helps gym owners stay on track with their financial goals. 

First, identify fixed costs such as rent, utilities, and payroll, which are necessary and predictable expenses. 

Next, estimate variable costs, including [marketing](https://zenplanner.com/product/gym-marketing-software/) and equipment maintenance, which may fluctuate. 

Then, set aside an emergency fund to cover unforeseen expenses like repairs or unexpected drops in membership. 

Finally, regularly review your budget to ensure it aligns with your financial goals, making adjustments as necessary. 

#### [**Read more for the** **Five Key Financials Tips for Opening a Gym**](https://zenplanner.com/financial/five-key-financial-tips-for-opening-a-gym/)

## 5\. Membership Growth and Forecasting

Accurate [membership sales forecasting](https://zenplanner.com/product/member-self-service/) is crucial for gym owners to project future revenue and plan for growth. By analyzing historical data and market trends, owners can make informed decisions about class schedules, staffing, and promotional efforts, optimizing resources to increase profitability. This critical process helps gyms anticipate demand, adjust offerings, and prepare for seasonal fluctuations. 

Additionally, forecasting enables gym owners to allocate marketing budgets effectively. By understanding where potential growth lies, gyms can target their campaigns more precisely and see better returns on investment. 

In summary, a robust membership sales forecasting strategy ensures that gym decisions are data-driven, paving the way for sustainable growth and financial stability. By leveraging [Zen Planner’s](http://www.zenplanner.com/) tools, gym owners can harness valuable insights, streamline operations, and confidently navigate their business growth.

Securing a favorable lease plays a crucial role in laying the groundwork for your gym’s success and long-term viability. Thoroughly evaluating these factors will help ensure a stable foundation for your gym operations.

# How to Make Your Fitness Business Stand Out on Google

[Home](https://member.afsfitness.com/)

![How to Make Your Fitness Business Stand Out on Google](https://member.afsfitness.com/sites/default/files/Tim%20May24%20blog.jpg)

![](/sites/default/files/Tim%20M_headshot.png)_By Tim Mauk__, Special FBA Contributor_

It is no secret that Google is a massive driver of leads for gyms and personal training studios worldwide. However, for many small- to medium-sized fitness facilities, the prospect of getting their website on the first page of a Google results page seems lofty.

Fortunately, local search engine optimization (SEO) can be a huge asset for these owners to leverage when utilizing the strategic advantage of proximity to their ideal clients.

In this blog, we will discuss local SEO, how it differs from general SEO, and some great tools you can use to position yourself favorably in your local market.

### What is SEO VS Local SEO

Search engine optimization (SEO) is the craft of designing, editing, and structuring information so search engines can easily find, review, and catalog/index it. Further refinement of website pages and various surrounding elements can inform indexers on how your information relates to queries from a relevancy, authority, and topical expertise (among other things) standpoint. [Search Engine Land](https://searchengineland.com/guide/what-is-seo) concisely summarizes SEO as “the process of improving your website to increase its visibility in Google, Microsoft Bing, and other search engines…”

Similarly, local SEO operates on the same principles. However, the geographic location and a few other location-based variables play a more significant role in search result specificity. One of the most common features referenced when talking about local SEO is the Google Map Pack, which lists relevant local businesses in the Google Map SERP (search engine results page) features section on queries like “personal training studios near me.”

### Popular Local SEO Tools for Fitness Professionals

Due to the complexities involved and seemingly constant large algorithm changes from search engine providers, many businesses assume SEO optimization is not a project they want to take on. Luckily, when looking at local SEO, there are some straightforward things you can start incorporating into your fitness business that can help move the dial on your local listing rank.

**Google Business Profile**

One of the most basic starting points is [claiming or establishing their Google Business Profile](https://gymsplash.com/learning/marketing/claiming-and-building-your-gyms-google-business-profile/). In short, this is a free tool that Google offers that allows inquiring searchers to quickly review critical business information straight from their search results page without having to click on your website. Information like business hours, phone numbers, addresses, and more can be easily found and displayed here alongside reviews and photos of your facility. This completed profile can be an excellent opportunity to market your facility through accurate and clean information, appealing pictures, answers to questions, and positive reviews.

**Reviews**

Everybody knows reviews are influential. However, there are some gold nuggets into “how” you collect and further leverage your reviews for additional value. First, implementing a system of asking happy clients and members for reviews - and then making it easy for them to access and write a review is pivotal to the long-term growth of your reviews. This organic and consistent growth trend of reviews can be a powerful indicator for search engines, especially with local SEO.

Further, once you receive reviews (especially on Google), responding as the facility's owner with a personalized note to reviews can also give you an additional boost and an opportunity to pepper in other keywords you would like to rank for. Additionally, adding reviews to your website can help build further on-page SEO value.

**Website Local References**

Another factor in the local SEO ranking is helping the bots understand your location and authority within the geographic area. Adding links to popular local businesses or pages and referencing popular nearby locations can aid this process. Some fitness businesses accomplish this via individual posts within their blog, or they may add popular nearby companies to their “directions page.” Others have even made a “local partners” page listing businesses they partner with nearby. There is no specific way you “have” to follow to implement this sort of information, but focusing on doing it in a way that feels organic for your website/business and also could benefit your clients is always a recommended best practice.

### Stand Out Locally

Outside of the primarily digital topics outlined above, there are some other considerations to review that can also help from a local SEO perspective. [Local news and press releases](https://gymsplash.com/local-news-and-press-releases-can-help-your-fitness-studio/) are still powerful tools for regional markets. Focusing on highlighting the newsworthy opportunities that exist (or developing them), you can help drive a fantastic awareness opportunity within your local geographic area for significantly less cost than advertising the same medium. And because those types of mentions typically get published online with additional contact information, you also help build a more robust local backlink profile for your business.

Another opportunity to drive brand impressions and interact with the community is to sign up for local (and relevant) events and programs. These are great ways to meet with the community, talk about your brand and network, or even learn about other nearby businesses you could start a partnership with. Again, activities like these can add local SEO value by writing an event recap blog on your website.

### Final Thoughts

Local SEO should not be a scary concept for fitness facility owners. Many of the ways we discussed that you can help move the dial on your local rankings are generally good business sense to-dos. You can also further process content from these initiatives for your marketing purposes—such as additional content for social media from images from events or blog announcements.
